questions.question: How does Anna describe her first sensations after the injury?
answers: She feels only physical pain
She feels her own body is alien and that the hand doesn't belong to her
She immediately remembers the whole accident
She has no psychological symptoms at all
questions.explanation: The opening scenes focus on the disturbed sense of her own body.

questions.question: Why does Dr Marek propose micro-phenomenology?
answers: To measure her blood pressure
To study the structure of Anna's experience, not just the scan results
To replace the MRI
To teach her religious meditation
questions.explanation: The method is meant to help describe the experience of consciousness and perception itself.

questions.question: What idea does Marta contribute in the talk about illusion and the 'self'?
answers: That such questions are meaningless
That even if experience is an illusion, it still remains lived as one's own and real
That all machines should be switched off immediately
That consciousness is purely religion
questions.explanation: Marta stresses the importance of the experience being one's own, even if it is a mental construction.

questions.question: How does Dr Marek distinguish intelligence and consciousness?
answers: He treats them as the same thing
He says intelligence can exist without subjective feeling
He claims consciousness is easily measurable
He considers AI already fully conscious
questions.explanation: This is a key ethical theme in the conversation about AI.

questions.question: What conclusion does Anna reach in the epilogue?
answers: That she has found the definitive definition of consciousness
That the question of the 'self' may matter more than a ready answer
That she no longer wants to write about science
That the injury changed nothing for her
questions.explanation: The ending leaves the problem open and stresses the importance of the question itself.
